# Configuring a Local LLM Provider

To point the terminal app at a local LLM using an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set the `OPENAI_API_BASE_URL` environment variable and provide a dummy API key (local servers typically skip authentication).
```toml[llm]
provider = "openai-compatible"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1"
model = "llama3.1"
api_key = "sk-dummy-key"
```
Replace `base_url` with the address of your chosen server — common defaults include `http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1` (llama.cpp / text-generation-webui), `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1` (vLLM), and `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` (Ollama). The `model` field should match the model your server exposes; check its console or run `curl http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/models` to list available models.

## Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Connection refused` | Verify the server is running; check the port and bind address (`0.0.0.0` vs `127.0.0.1`). |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Some servers still require a key — set `api_key` to any non-empty string. |
| `Model not found` | Confirm the model name matches what the server loaded; list models via the `/v1/models` endpoint. |
| Slow responses | Reduce `max_tokens` or use a smaller model; ensure the server has enough GPU/CPU memory. |
| TLS errors when using `https://` | Switch to `http://` for localhost, or add the server's self-signed certificate to your trust store. |
| Garbled or truncated output | Increase `max_tokens`; check the server's context-length limit and raise it if needed. |After editing the configuration, restart the terminal app so the new settings take effect.
